leftEvidence.title: Household, circumcision, unbroken bones, and one law define participation

points.label: Question
points.left: The ordinance begins as direct instruction about who may eat.
points.right: Excluded men bring a concrete question to Moses.

points.label: Flexibility
points.left: The meal stays in one house and its bones remain unbroken.
points.right: The date may move for impurity or travel while meal rules remain.

points.label: Foreigner
points.left: A circumcised resident foreigner may keep it under one law.
points.right: The foreigner who desires to keep it follows the same statute.

payload.posture: Keep each Scripture witness intact, inspect what each states, and do not supply a combined sequence the sources do not author.

rightEvidence.title: Impurity, distance, second-month timing, and one statute answer an interruption

payload.tension: Both passages preserve obligation and shared statute while addressing different reasons a person may stand outside the meal.
payload.title: Participation, delay, and one statute
